files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Accounts.Account
files.Summary: Returns information and links relating to a single account.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Accounts.IAccountId
files.Summary: Represents a Stellar account identifier, providing access to the account's public key, address, and signing key. Implemented by both standard and accounts.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Accounts.ITransactionBuilderAccount
files.Summary: Represents a Stellar account used for building transactions. Provides access to the account's key pair, sequence number management, and muxed account information needed by .

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Accounts.KeyPair
files.Summary: Represents the public (and optionally secret) keys of a Stellar account, providing methods for signing data, verifying signatures, and encoding/decoding account identifiers.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Accounts.MuxedAccount
files.Summary: Provides factory methods for creating account identifiers from XDR muxed account representations.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Accounts.MuxedAccountMed25519
files.Summary: Represents a multiplexed (muxed) Stellar account that combines an Ed25519 public key with a 64-bit numeric identifier. Muxed accounts allow a single Stellar account to distinguish between multiple virtual accounts (e.g., for custodial services) without requiring separate on-ledger accounts. Addresses for muxed accounts start with "M".

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Amount
files.Summary: Utility class for converting between Stellar amount representations. Stellar stores amounts as 64-bit integers with 7 decimal places of precision (1 XLM = 10,000,000 stroops).

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.Asset
files.Summary: Asset class represents an asset, either the native asset (XLM) or a asset code / issuer account ID pair. An asset code describes an asset code and issuer pair. In the case of the native asset XLM, the issuer will be null.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.AssetAmount
files.Summary: Class to have Asset and Amount in the same place.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.AssetExtensions
files.Summary: Provides extension methods for the class.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum
files.Summary: Assets are uniquely identified by the asset code and the issuer. Ultimately, it’s up to the issuer to set the asset code. By convention, however, currencies should be represented by the appropriate ISO 4217 code. For stocks and bonds, use the appropriate ISIN number.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum12
files.Summary: Represents a Stellar credit asset with an alphanumeric code between 5 and 12 characters long.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum4
files.Summary: Represents a Stellar credit asset with an alphanumeric code between 1 and 4 characters long.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.AssetTypeNative
files.Summary: Represents the native Stellar asset (XLM/Lumens). This is the built-in currency of the Stellar network.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.ChangeTrustAsset.Wrapper
files.Summary: Wraps a standard instance as a , enabling non-pool-share assets to be used in change trust operations.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.ChangeTrustAsset
files.Summary: Represents an asset that can be used in a ChangeTrust operation. This includes standard Stellar assets (native, credit_alphanum4, credit_alphanum12) and liquidity pool shares.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.LiquidityPoolShareChangeTrustAsset
files.Summary: Represents a liquidity pool share asset used in change trust operations. This asset type allows accounts to establish trustlines to liquidity pools on the Stellar network.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.LiquidityPoolShareTrustlineAsset
files.Summary: Represents a liquidity pool share as a trustline asset. This is used to reference an existing liquidity pool trustline by its pool ID.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.TrustlineAsset.Wrapper
files.Summary: Wraps a standard instance as a , enabling non-pool-share assets to be used where a trustline asset is required.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Assets.TrustlineAsset
files.Summary: Represents an asset that can appear in a trustline on the Stellar network. This includes standard assets (native, credit_alphanum4, credit_alphanum12) and liquidity pool shares.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Base32Encoding.Base32EncodingOptions
files.Summary: Options for controlling Base32 encoding behavior.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Base32Encoding
files.Summary: Provides RFC 4648 Base32 encoding and decoding methods. Used internally by for encoding and decoding Stellar keys and identifiers.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.ClaimAtom
files.Summary: Represents a single trade that was executed during a path payment or offer operation on the Stellar network. Each claim atom contains the assets and amounts exchanged.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.ClaimAtomLiquidityPool
files.Summary: Represents a claim atom from a liquidity pool trade on the Stellar network. Contains the liquidity pool ID and the assets and amounts exchanged.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.ClaimAtomOrderBook
files.Summary: Represents a claim atom from an order book trade on the Stellar decentralized exchange. Contains the seller, offer ID, and the assets and amounts exchanged.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.ClaimAtomV0
files.Summary: Represents a V0 claim atom from a trade on the Stellar network. This is the original format that identifies the seller by their Ed25519 public key rather than a full account ID.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.ClaimableBalanceIdUtils
files.Summary: Utility methods for converting between different representations of Stellar claimable balance IDs (base32 B..., hex 0000..., and XDR).

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicate
files.Summary: Represents a claim predicate for building claimable balance operations in Stellar transactions.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicateAnd
files.Summary: Represents a logical AND combination of two claim predicates. A claimable balance can be claimed only when both the left and right predicates are satisfied.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicateBeforeAbsoluteTime
files.Summary: Represents a claim predicate that is valid only before a specified absolute point in time. The claimable balance can be claimed only before the given Unix timestamp.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicateBeforeRelativeTime
files.Summary: Represents a claim predicate that is valid only before a specified duration has elapsed since the claimable balance was created. The duration is measured in seconds.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicateNot
files.Summary: Represents a logical NOT (negation) of a claim predicate. A claimable balance can be claimed only when the inner predicate is not satisfied.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicateOr
files.Summary: Represents a logical OR combination of two claim predicates. A claimable balance can be claimed when either the left or right predicate (or both) is satisfied.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.ClaimPredicateUnconditional
files.Summary: Represents an unconditional claim predicate that is always satisfied. A claimable balance with this predicate can be claimed at any time without restrictions.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Claimants.Claimant
files.Summary: Represents a claimant for building claimable balance operations in Stellar transactions.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.AccountNotFoundException
files.Summary: Thrown when trying to load an account that doesn't exist on the Stellar network.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.AccountRequiresMemoException
files.Summary: AccountRequiresMemoException is thrown when a transaction is trying to submit a payment operation to an account that requires a memo. See SEP0029: https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0029.md

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.AssetCodeLengthInvalidException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when a Stellar asset code exceeds the allowed length (1-4 characters for AlphaNum4 or 5-12 characters for AlphaNum12).

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.ClientProtocolException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when an HTTP client protocol error occurs while communicating with a Stellar server.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.ExternalRefNotFoundException
files.Summary: Thrown when the CAP-85 executable tag entry that an external executable reference points at cannot be used: it does not exist, or it has been archived and must be restored before the reference resolves again.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.FormatException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when the format of a Stellar SDK value (such as a key, address, or encoded data) is invalid.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.MemoTooLongException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when a transaction memo exceeds the maximum allowed length (28 bytes for text memos, 32 bytes for hash and return memos).

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.NoNetworkSelectedException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when an operation requiring a Stellar network (such as signing a transaction) is attempted before a network (e.g., public or testnet) has been configured via Network.Use.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.NotEnoughSignaturesException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when a Stellar transaction has no signatures and at least one is required to produce a valid transaction envelope.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.ServiceUnavailableException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when the Stellar Horizon server returns an HTTP 503 Service Unavailable response, indicating the server is temporarily overloaded or undergoing maintenance.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.SorobanRpcException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when the Stellar RPC server answers a request with a JSON-RPC error object (JSON-RPC 2.0 §5.1) instead of a result. Such a response carries no result member and normally arrives with HTTP status 200, so it is distinct from the HTTP-level failures reported by , , and .

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.SubmitTransactionTimeoutResponseException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when the Stellar Horizon server returns an HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout response to a transaction submission, indicating the upstream Stellar Core node did not respond in time.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.SubmitTransactionUnknownResponseException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when the Stellar Horizon server returns an unexpected or unrecognized HTTP status code in response to a transaction submission.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.TooManyRequestsException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when the Stellar Horizon server returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response, indicating the client has exceeded the rate limit for its IP address.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Exceptions.TooManySignaturesException
files.Summary: The exception that is thrown when attempting to create an unsigned transaction envelope from a transaction that already has signatures.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Federation.ConnectionErrorException

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Federation.Federation

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Federation.FederationServer

For resolving a stellar address without knowing which federation server to query use Federation#resolve(String). See Federation docs: https://www.stellar.org/developers/learn/concepts/federation.html

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Federation.ServerErrorException

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Federation.StellarTomlNotFoundInvalidException

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Requests.RetryingHttpMessageHandler
files.Summary:
HTTP message handler that implements retry logic for connection failures (network errors, DNS failures, etc.) and for configured HTTP status codes (see ). Honors the Retry-After response header when is true. By default, only safe HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are retried on status codes; connection-failure (exception) retries apply to all methods.

Retries re-send the same instance, so request bodies must be re-readable, buffered content (StringContent, ByteArrayContent, FormUrlEncodedContent — all of the SDK's own requests qualify). A non-seekable StreamContent body fails on the second attempt.

Cancellations are never retried: when HttpClient.Timeout fires it cancels the request's token, so the resulting propagates immediately, exactly like a user-initiated cancellation.

files.Summary: Represents an offer on the Stellar decentralized exchange. An offer is a bid or ask to exchange one asset for another at a specified price.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.AccountMergeOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents an account_merge operation response. Merges one account into another, transferring all XLM balance and deleting the source account.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.AllowTrustOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents an allow_trust operation response (deprecated operation). Allows another account to hold an asset issued by the source account.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.BeginSponsoringFutureReservesOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a begin_sponsoring_future_reserves operation response. This operation establishes a sponsorship relationship where the source account sponsors the reserves (minimum balance requirements) for operations performed by another account until an end_sponsoring_future_reserves operation is encountered.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.BumpSequenceOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a bump_sequence operation response. Bumps forward the sequence number of the source account to the specified value.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ChangeTrustOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a change_trust operation response. Creates, updates, or deletes a trustline between accounts.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ClaimClaimableBalanceOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a claim_claimable_balance operation response. Claims a claimable balance, transferring the balance to the claimant's account. The claimant must be one of the claimants specified when the balance was created, and their predicate conditions must be met.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ClawbackClaimableBalanceOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a clawback_claimable_balance operation response. Claws back (destroys) a claimable balance, removing it from the network. This operation can only be performed by the asset issuer on claimable balances containing assets that have the clawback-enabled flag set. The claimable balance and its assets are permanently removed.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ClawbackOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a clawback operation response. Claws back (burns) a specified amount of an asset from an account. This operation can only be performed by the asset issuer on assets that have the clawback-enabled flag set. The clawed back amount is permanently removed from circulation.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.CreateAccountOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a create_account operation response. Creates and funds a new account with a starting balance of XLM.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.CreateClaimableBalanceOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a create_claimable_balance operation response. Creates a claimable balance that can be claimed by one or more claimants according to specified predicates. The balance is held by the network and can be claimed when the predicate conditions are met.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.CreatePassiveOfferOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a create_passive_sell_offer operation response. Creates an offer to sell an asset that does not take another offer of equal price when created. Unlike active offers, passive offers will not immediately match with existing offers at the same price.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.EndSponsoringFutureReservesOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents an end_sponsoring_future_reserves operation response. This operation terminates the current sponsorship relationship established by a begin_sponsoring_future_reserves operation. It must be submitted by the sponsored account to complete the sponsorship sandwich.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ExtendFootprintOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents an extend_footprint_ttl operation response. Extends the time-to-live (TTL) of Soroban contract data entries.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.InflationOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents an inflation operation response (deprecated operation). Runs the weekly inflation process and distributes new lumens.

files.Summary: The type of muxed ID for the destination account.

files.Summary: Represents a parameter passed to a host function.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.InvokeHostFunctionOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents an invoke_host_function operation response. Invokes a Soroban smart contract function on the Stellar network.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.LiquidityPoolDepositOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a liquidity_pool_deposit operation response. Deposits assets into a liquidity pool in exchange for pool shares.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.LiquidityPoolWithdrawOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a liquidity_pool_withdraw operation response. Withdraws assets from a liquidity pool by burning pool shares.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ManageBuyOfferOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a manage_buy_offer operation response. Creates, updates, or deletes an offer to buy a specific amount of an asset at a given price.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ManageDataOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a manage_data operation response. Sets, modifies, or deletes a data entry (key-value pair) associated with an account.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ManageOfferOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a manage_offer operation response. Creates, updates, or deletes an offer to buy or sell assets on the Stellar decentralized exchange. This is the base class for both manage_sell_offer and manage_buy_offer operations.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.ManageSellOfferOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a manage_sell_offer operation response. Creates, updates, or deletes an offer to sell a specific amount of an asset at a given price.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.OperationResponse
files.Summary: Base class for all operation responses. Operations are actions that mutate the ledger, such as creating accounts or making payments. See: Operations

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.OperationResponseLinks
files.Summary: The response is for the genesis ledger of the Stellar network, and the links in the _links attribute provide links to other relevant resources in Horizon. The key of each link specifies that links relation to the current resource, and transactions means “Transactions that occurred in this operation”. The transactions link is also templated, which means that the href attribute of the link is actually a URI template, as specified by RFC 6570. We use URI templates to show you what parameters a give resource can take.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.PathPaymentStrictReceiveOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a path_payment_strict_receive operation response. Sends an amount in a specific asset to a destination account through a path of offers. The receive amount is specified, and the send amount can vary.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.PathPaymentStrictSendOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a path_payment_strict_send operation response. Sends an amount in a specific asset to a destination account through a path of offers. The send amount is specified, and the receive amount can vary.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.PaymentOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a payment operation response. Sends an amount in a specific asset from one account to another.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.RestoreFootprintOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a restore_footprint operation response. Restores archived Soroban contract data entries back to the active state.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.RevokeSponsorshipOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a revoke_sponsorship operation response. This operation removes or transfers sponsorship of reserves for various ledger entries (accounts, trustlines, offers, data, signers, or claimable balances). Only one set of fields will be populated depending on the type of sponsorship being revoked.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.SetOptionsOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a set_options operation response. Sets various options for an account, such as signers, thresholds, flags, and home domain.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Responses.Operations.SetTrustlineFlagsOperationResponse
files.Summary: Represents a set_trustline_flags operation response. Sets flags on a trustline, controlling authorization states for an asset.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Sep.Sep0001.StellarToml
files.Summary:
Parses and provides access to stellar.toml files as defined in SEP-0001. The stellar.toml file is a standardized configuration file that organizations publish at https://DOMAIN/.well-known/stellar.toml to provide information about their Stellar integration, including service endpoints, validators, currencies, and organizational details. See SEP-0001

HttpClient Usage: For production code, it is strongly recommended to pass a shared instance to the static methods ( and , each with an overload that also takes resilience options). If no HttpClient is provided, a new instance will be created and disposed for each call, which is inefficient and can lead to socket exhaustion under load. Create and reuse a single HttpClient instance (or use IHttpClientFactory) for multiple calls to these methods.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Sep.Sep0024.InteractiveService
files.Summary:
Implements SEP-0024 v3.8.0 - Hosted Deposit and Withdrawal for Stellar anchors. SEP-0024 defines a standard protocol for anchors to facilitate deposits and withdrawals using an interactive web interface. This allows users to convert between Stellar assets and fiat currencies or other external assets. The interactive flow works as follows:

  1. Client authenticates with SEP-10 WebAuth to get a JWT token
  2. Client calls the deposit or withdraw endpoint with asset and amount
  3. Server returns a URL for an interactive web interface
  4. Client displays the URL in a popup/webview where user completes KYC
  5. User provides additional details (bank account, amounts, etc.)
  6. Server processes the transaction and updates status
  7. Client polls the transaction status endpoint for updates See SEP-0024

HttpClient Usage: For production code, it is strongly recommended to pass a shared instance to the constructor or . If no HttpClient is provided, a new instance will be created internally. While implements to clean up internal clients, reusing a single HttpClient instance (or using IHttpClientFactory) is more efficient and avoids socket exhaustion under load.

IDisposable and HttpClient ownership

If you pass an external into the constructor or , that client remains owned by the caller. In that case, disposing will not dispose the external client, and you are responsible for managing the lifecycle yourself (for example, by reusing a single long-lived instance for performance and resilience).

You can configure retry policies, timeouts, and circuit breaker behavior by passing to the constructor or . These options are only used when creating an internal . If you provide your own , the resilience options are ignored.

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Sep.Sep0024.Requests.DepositRequest
files.Summary: Request to initiate an interactive deposit flow with an anchor. A deposit allows a user to send external assets (fiat via bank transfer, BTC, USD cash, etc.) to an anchor, which then sends an equivalent amount of the Stellar asset (minus fees) to the user's Stellar account. The deposit endpoint returns an interactive URL where the user completes KYC, provides payment details, and receives instructions for sending their off-chain assets to the anchor. Authentication: Always required. Must provide a SEP-10 JWT token.

This request allows clients to query the exact fee that would be charged for a specific deposit or withdrawal operation. This endpoint is optional for anchors that can fully express their fee structure in the /info response using fee_fixed, fee_percent, and fee_minimum fields. Authentication: Required if feeEndpointInfo.authenticationRequired is true in the /info response. Provide a SEP-10 JWT token in the Jwt property.

At least one of Id, StellarTransactionId, or ExternalTransactionId must be provided. Authentication: Always required. Must provide a SEP-10 JWT token.

The user sends the Stellar asset to the anchor, and the anchor sends the equivalent off-chain asset (minus fees) to the user. The withdrawal endpoint returns an interactive URL where the user completes KYC, provides bank account or wallet details, and receives instructions for the withdrawal. Authentication: Always required. Must provide a SEP-10 JWT token.

Represents a single deposit or withdrawal transaction with an anchor. Contains comprehensive information about the transaction status, amounts, fees, and relevant identifiers for tracking the transaction through its lifecycle. Transaction statuses:

  • incomplete: Additional user action required via the interactive URL
  • pending_user_transfer_start: Waiting for user to initiate transfer
  • pending_anchor: Anchor is processing the transaction
  • pending_stellar: Transaction submitted to Stellar network
  • pending_external: Pending external payment system
  • pending_trust: Waiting for user to establish trustline
  • pending_user: Waiting for user action
  • completed: Transaction successfully completed
  • refunded: Transaction was refunded
  • expired: Transaction expired before completion
  • error: Transaction failed with an error

files.Title: StellarDotnetSdk.Sep.Sep0038.QuoteService
files.Summary:
Client for SEP-0038 v2.5.0 — Anchor RFQ API. Lets a wallet discover which assets an anchor exchanges, fetch indicative prices, and request firm quotes whose id it then passes as quote_id to a SEP-6, SEP-24 or SEP-31 transaction. See SEP-0038.

Authentication

, and accept an optional JWT, which the anchor may use to personalize the response. and require one. Obtain it with SEP-10 () for G.../M... accounts or SEP-45 () for contract accounts.

Amounts

Amounts and prices are values. Requests send them as invariant-culture strings, keeping the scale given; responses are read exactly: a value that cannot hold without rounding fails with rather than being approximated.

Errors

Invalid arguments — including the sell/buy amount exclusivity rules, a zero or negative amount, a string property that is empty or whitespace rather than null, and a JWT that is not printable ASCII without whitespace — throw from the returned task, before anything is sent. Error responses map to (400), (403), (404) and (anything else, including a 3xx, or an unusable success body); all derive from . A Retry-After header on an error response (typically 429 or 503) is exposed as 's . Response bodies are read up to 1 MiB, and parsed with the SDK's hardened JSON options, which reject duplicated mapped properties. An error body over the limit is dropped ( and are then null) but the status still selects the exception type; a success body over the limit raises . A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped.

A success body is also checked against the request: a firm quote must carry a usable id, the requested asset pair, no delivery method other than the one requested (compared without regard to case), and an expiry no earlier than the requested expire_after; prices and amounts must be greater than zero, and a decimals count must not be negative. A response that fails these checks raises , whose still holds what the anchor sent (for POST /quote, the id of the quote it already created).

Transport failures surface as (including a connection that drops while a success body is being read) or (cancellation, or a timeout, in which case its inner exception is a ). The whole exchange — headers and body — is bounded by the of the client in use (and, for the internal client, by ), so a server that trickles its body cannot stall the caller. An internal client with set throws Polly's BrokenCircuitException while the circuit is open, and a call on a disposed service that owns its client throws . On runtimes before .NET 10, a request whose URL exceeds the runtime's length limit (a quote id tens of kilobytes long) raises .

Redirects

The internal client does not follow redirects, so a 3xx answer raises and a request is never replayed to another host. A caller-owned client follows redirects if its handler does; the service then rejects any response that comes from a different origin than the quote server, but by that point the request, its body and the custom headers have already been sent there (on .NET's SocketsHttpHandler, not the JWT, whose Authorization header it drops on a redirect). Only the final location is visible, so a chain that leaves the origin and returns to it is not detected at all. Disable AllowAutoRedirect on a caller-owned client's handler to avoid both. The check compares the final request URI, so a caller's handler that rewrites it to another origin (a gateway, for example) is rejected the same way.

Retries

POST /quote is not idempotent: every call creates a new firm quote that the anchor holds in reserve until it expires. Do not pass or : both retry POST on a 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504 answer, so one call can reserve two quotes. Use (which still replays a POST whose response was lost in transit) or .

HttpClient ownership

Pass a shared (or one from IHttpClientFactory) in production; it stays owned by the caller and is not disposed with this service. When none is passed, the service creates its own, configured by , and disposes it in .
